characteristics.cultivar: Camellia sinensis var. sinensis, primarily clonal selections

description.short: Bold, jet-black, full-bodied low-grown Ceylon tea — the richest and thickest in cup of all Sri Lankan regions
description.overview: Southern coastal lowlands where hot, humid tropical climates accelerate rapid bush growth, concentrating deep caramel sugars and creating heavy, velvety body.
description.leaf: Jet-black, twisted leaves or small granular CTC pellets
description.taste: Bold, thick, deeply malty with chocolate and caramel notes, standing up effortlessly to milk and sweetening
description.processing: Plucking → withering → orthodox or CTC rolling → deep full oxidation → drying

history.origin: Named after the ancient historic southern kingdom of Ruhuna, dating back to pre-Buddhist Sri Lankan antiquity.
history.development: Low-grown cultivation expanded dynamically in the late 19th and early 20th centuries as demand for heavy, strong breakfast teas grew globally.
history.modern: Today Ruhuna is the largest volume producer in Sri Lanka, revered across the Middle East and Central Asia for its dark liquor and bold flavor.
interestingFacts: 'Low-grown' is an official regulatory tier of Ceylon tea (below 600 m), and Ruhuna is its most famous exemplar.
Because of its dark liquor and rich sweetness, Ruhuna tea commands immense popularity across the Middle East, where extra-strong, sweet black tea is a hospitality staple.
